meta: Same clog every few months? Hydro jetting scours roots, grease and scale from larger lines, with a clear price first in Oakley, CA. Call (888) 910-8644.
lead: Hydro jetting in Oakley, CA uses a pressurized water stream to scrub the inside of a drain or sewer pipe, not just punch a hole through the clog.
It suits lines that keep filling back up, once a camera shows the pipe is sound enough to take it.
intro: Hydro jetting is a cleaning method in which a hose with a rotating nozzle sends high-pressure water forward and backward along a pipe, stripping grease, scale, silt and fine roots from the walls. It works best on 3-inch to 6-inch lines, such as a kitchen branch, a laundry drain or the sewer lateral running to the Ironhouse Sanitary District main.

Below you will find the signs of a line that needs more than a cable, what the process looks like, when we decline to jet, and what shapes the price. Routine fixture clogs are handled by our [[drain-cleaning|drain cleaning]] service.

sections.h2: My drain keeps clogging again, even after it gets cleared
paras: When a line opens up with a snake and then slows down again within weeks or months, the cable usually removed only the middle of the blockage. A film of grease, mineral scale or root hair stays on the pipe wall and catches the next batch of debris.

The technical name for the fix is hydro jetting. It cleans the full circle of the pipe instead of drilling a narrow hole, which is why it is the usual answer to a repeat clog in a main or a long branch.

sections.h2: Backed up today and a jet might be the answer
paras: A sewage backup, a toilet that will not clear or a floor drain bubbling up is an emergency whatever the eventual method. Our dispatch is open 24/7, and we decide at the cleanout whether a cable can open the line first or whether the line needs jetting. While you wait, reduce what goes into the pipe.
do_now: Stop using sinks, showers, the dishwasher and the washer until the line is clear.
Do not flush a backed-up toilet again, since each flush pushes more water toward the lowest opening in the house.
Find your cleanout cap outside, if you know where it is, and tell us whether it is accessible or buried.
Keep children, pets and bare feet away from any floor where sewage has surfaced.
Photograph affected areas for your records before towels and cleanup change the scene.

sections.h2: What happens inside the pipe during a jetting visit
paras: A technician opens the cleanout and feeds a hose with a small nozzle into the line. Water exits the nozzle through jets angled backward, which pulls the hose forward and makes the nozzle spin. On the way back, the operator slows down over trouble spots and works the nozzle back and forth.

Different nozzles do different jobs. A penetrating nozzle drills through a hard plug, a rotating nozzle scours scale and grease off the walls, and a root-cutting nozzle shaves roots from joints. The flow carries debris toward the district sewer, and we usually run a camera afterward to confirm what is left.

sections.h2: Which lines are candidates for jetting
paras: Jetting earns its cost where a cable can only do a partial job. These are the situations where we usually recommend it.

items.d: Years of cooking fat form a layered coating that only moving water at pressure will remove completely.
A root-cutting nozzle clears the hairs and thicker strands that a cable head tends to push aside.
Hard deposits narrow the opening over time, and a jet can restore much of the original diameter.
Cleaning the whole wall resets the clock, and many homeowners then book a periodic cleaning.

sections.h2: Jetting or cabling: how the two methods differ on the same pipe
paras: Both methods are legitimate, and neither is better in every case. The right choice depends on what is coating the pipe and what shape the pipe is in.

sections.h2: When we say no to jetting, and what happens instead
paras: Water at high pressure is not appropriate for every pipe. A line with a crack, a separated joint or a section that has dropped out of line can lose water into the soil, undermine the ground around it, or widen the damage. We will not jet a pipe that a camera shows to be failing.

If the camera finds that kind of damage, the conversation shifts to the repair options on our [[sewer-line-repair|sewer line repair]] page, which include spot repair and trenchless lining. A clean, sound pipe is the starting point for lining, so jetting and repair often follow each other in sequence.

sections.h2: What goes into the price of hydro jetting
paras: Jetting requires heavier equipment than a cable, so it is priced differently. You receive a clear price before work starts, based on what we can see and what you describe.

factors.t: Length and diameter of the line
factors.d: More pipe and a larger bore mean more time and more water.
A good cleanout speeds things up. Without one, we may need to pull a toilet or find another opening.
Light grease needs one pass. Layered scale or dense roots need several, with nozzle changes.
A look before confirms the pipe can take the pressure, and a look afterward shows the result.
Night, weekend and holiday dispatch carries different labor costs than a daytime appointment.

sections.insurance: Homeowner policies often do not pay to clean a line that has built up slowly, since that is treated as maintenance. Sudden damage from a backup may be covered under some policies, so ask your insurer and keep photos and any camera footage to support a claim.
sections.call_line: Call (888) 910-8644 with the history of the clog, and we will explain which method is likely to fit and what it involves.

sections.h2: The Oakley lateral: who owns the line you are jetting
paras: A jetted lateral is the owner's line, and the District's responsibility begins at the public main the lateral joins. If it overflows, the cleanup and any damage are yours to handle. Jetting that lateral is therefore a decision you make, and a camera recording of the finished job is a useful record to keep.
Jetting does not change what the state plumbing code (the California Plumbing Code, drawn from the UPC), requires of a sound drain line, which is why a camera check comes first.

faqs.q: Do you handle hydro jetting emergencies at night or on weekends in Oakley?
a: Yes. Dispatch is open 24/7. For a backup, we usually clear the blockage first and discuss jetting once water is moving, since the pipe needs a camera look before high pressure goes in. If the line is still draining, a same-day slot may be open.

faqs.q: What is hydro jetting and how is it different from snaking?
a: Snaking opens a channel through the clog with a rotating cable. Jetting uses a hose and pressurized water to clean the full wall of the pipe. Our [[drain-cleaning|drain cleaning]] page covers the cable side in detail.

faqs.q: Why does my line clog every few months?
a: Repeat clogs often come from a coating that stays on the pipe after a cable pass, such as grease, scale or fine roots. Jetting addresses the coating, and a camera can show whether the pipe has a defect that keeps catching debris.

faqs.q: Is jetting safe for old pipes?
a: It depends on the condition of the pipe, not just its age. A camera inspection first tells us whether the walls and joints can handle the pressure. If they cannot, we do not jet.
A root-cutting nozzle removes roots inside the pipe. It does not stop them from growing back through the same joint, so a recurring root problem may call for a repair or lining.

faqs.q: Does a home sale inspection recommendation mean I have to jet?
a: Not by itself. In the Ironhouse Sanitary District, the sale of a property more than 20 years old can trigger a required camera inspection and Compliance Certificate, so ask your agent and the district what applies. Jetting is only worth doing if the camera shows buildup.

cta_mid: A line that fills back up after every cable visit is a good candidate for a wall-cleaning pass, so tell us how long the last fix held.
cta_end: Describe the last clog and how fast it came back, and we will tell you whether jetting fits your pipe.
